Also, increased liver echogenicity, intrahepatic bile duct dilation and hypersplenotrophy were detected by ultrasound examination. In addition, CT scanning confirmed the bilateral enlargement of the kidneys with cysts and the intrahepatic bile duct dilation (Fig. 1B).

Considering the involvement of genetic factor, the younger sister of the proband, a 6-year-old girl, was screened by urine routine tests. Unfortunately, she had microalbumin (362 mg/L) and hematuresis, although her renal function (eGFR 150.0 ml/min/1.73m2) was normal. No other abnormality was detected in laboratory tests including blood routine test, immunology test and liver function test. In addition, no abnormality was detected by abdominal ultrasound examination except punctuated echogenicity in the kidneys. However, CT scanning showed mild intrahepatic bile duct dilation (Fig. 1C).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Sagittal renal ultrasound of the right kidney of a neonate with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease, demonstrating diffuse renal hyperechogenicity and loss of corticomedullary differentiation, classic imaging findings of the disease. B: Sagittal renal ultrasound of the left kidney of the same neonate with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease, showing diffuse renal hyperechogenicity, loss of corticomedullary differentiation, and a small cyst (arrow) consistent with the disease's cystic manifestations.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Coronal T1 MRI demonstrates bilateral symmetric renal enlargement with altered parenchymal architecture and associated hepatic cystic lesions in a newborn with ARPKD. B: Sagittal T2 MRI shows an enlarged kidney with inverted (radial microcystic) structure and hepatic cystic lesions consistent with ARPKD.
